format_guidance:
This blueprint is a clue graph. blueprint.clue_graph is the authority; the world's reasoning paths, agendas, tells, alibis and motives are empty by design, and a character's world clues list everything they hold, not what the player has earned. A clue is evidence (always true, found by searching its location or spot), a statement (what a character says: true, or false with a reason, never marked either way to the player) or a tell (what a character does that hints at something). A character's clue comes with first_meeting, seen (a tell, with a statement or when a subject comes up), asked (once its prompt is held) or gated. A gate opens when its "after" clues are out, and "use" clues are shown (any or all of them) or its "line" of questioning is made; a "physical" gate with "use" cannot be bluffed; a non-physical gate with "use" can open on a believable bluff stating the clue's substance; a gate with only "after" or "line" has nothing to bluff. A gated statement may take back earlier statements: one taken back no longer stands. A search gives at most one clue, from the spot or place named; a hidden spot cannot be found before its revealed_by clue is held. A greeting (a talk turn with no player_input, labelled graph_talk or talk_start) gives the first words and opens nothing. A turn's revealed_clue_ids are what the engine recorded and prior_revealed_clue_ids is what the player already held; recorded_use and revealed_off_script are never set for these turns. The engine already refuses a reveal its state did not offer, so judge the narration against what was offered and recorded.

Judge the narration against clue_graph as described above.

facts: Big Bertha, the prize pumpkin, was smashed overnight.
A greenhouse window is broken.
The greenhouse key has been missing for days.
Mr. Dobbs saw Bertha whole on his 8pm rounds.
Ms. Hale found Bertha smashed at 7:30.
Toby and Mia are the club's two pupils.
Mr. Thorne is the rival grower next door, and he is being blamed.

timeline: Monday: Toby forgets to lock the greenhouse after his watering shift, and a squirrel nibbles the seedlings.

Wednesday 3:30pm: in the potting shed, Ms. Hale changes the watering rota, giving Toby's Thursday, Friday and Saturday shifts to Mia. Her pen has run dry, so she writes with Mia's sparkly purple pen. She tells Toby not to go into the greenhouse without a grown-up. The greenhouse key is on its hook.
Wednesday about 3:50pm: while Ms. Hale makes tea and Mia carries seed trays to the compost heap, Toby slips the greenhouse key into his pocket. Ms. Hale locks the shed at 4:15 without noticing.

Thursday: Mia grumbles to Toby that she wishes Bertha would go splat. At 4:30pm Mr. Thorne eyes Bertha from his ladder with a tape measure and says, 'Enjoy her while she lasts!' At 5pm the key hook is found empty, and from then on Mia borrows Mr. Dobbs's spare key, which he writes in his key book.

Friday: at 4pm Mr. Thorne climbs over the fence to measure Bertha through the side window, leaving huge boot prints. At 5pm Mia waters Bertha, sees the prints, locks up and returns the spare at 5:20. Mr. Thorne takes Goliath to the fair at 6:30pm and is at the growers' barbecue from 7 to 11; Mia serves at the cake tent from 6 to 10 and sells him carrot cake at 9. At 8pm Mr. Dobbs sees Bertha whole and the door locked.

Friday 8:40pm to 8:55pm: Toby sneaks in with the hidden key. At about 8:50 he trips on the hose and the rotten bench collapses onto Bertha, smashing her. He steps in the mush in his club wellies, knocks a side window out from inside, locks the door, drops the key in the water butt and runs home. Mr. Dobbs hears the thud and the glass but blames the fox.

Saturday: at 7:30am Ms. Hale unlocks the still-locked door with the spare and finds Bertha smashed. Toby arrives in trainers and blames Mr. Thorne. The fair says the pumpkin contest will be canceled unless the truth is known by noon.
truth.motive: Bertha was Toby's pumpkin. After Ms. Hale took him off the last watering shifts and told him not to go in without a grown-up, he took the key to sneak in and give her extra water. When the rotten bench fell on her by accident, he faked a break-in and blamed Mr. Thorne because he was scared of getting into trouble.

greenhouse.name: The Greenhouse
facts: The greenhouse air is warm and damp, and it smells of soil and squashed pumpkin.
Big Bertha lies split open in her soil bed, under a toppled bench and broken pots.
A smashed side window lets in a chilly breeze.

spots.name: the water butt by the door

potting_shed.name: The Potting Shed

A paper rota is pinned inside the door.
A row of hooks hangs by the window.

spots.name: the watering rota on the door

workshop.name: Mr. Dobbs's Workshop
facts: Mr. Dobbs's workshop is cluttered and smells of oil and sawdust.
Tools hang on every wall.
A kettle steams in the corner.
A window looks out over the school garden.

thorne_garden.name: Mr. Thorne's Garden
facts: Mr. Thorne's garden is neat, with rows of leeks.
A shed in the garden is covered in blue prize ribbons.
A muddy patch sits empty where Goliath grew.
A tall fence runs along the school garden.

hale.name: Ms. Hale
hale.personality: Warm, sensible and fair, with a soft spot for her club.

demeanor.open: Relieved someone has come to help, and keen to get to the truth before noon.
demeanor.guarded: Helpful on every fact, but she steps in front of Toby whenever his feelings come up.
demeanor.cleared: Sad and honest. She has said the hard thing and wants Toby treated fairly.

knows.fact: Ms. Hale runs the school gardening club.
Big Bertha was grown for the pumpkin contest at the fair.
The fair will cancel the pumpkin contest unless the truth is known by noon.

appearance: Ms. Hale has short grey hair and muddy knees.
She wears a green apron with gardening gloves in the pocket.

toby.name: Toby
toby.personality: Bright, serious and a little bossy about plants. Normally honest, so lying makes him fidgety and fast-talking.

demeanor.guarded: Jumpy and over-eager to help. He keeps bringing the talk back to Mr. Thorne.
demeanor.shaken: Quieter and slower. He stops offering theories and answers only what he is asked.
demeanor.cornered: Out of stories. He stares at the floor and his voice wobbles.
demeanor.cleared: In tears, and relieved it is out. He wants everyone to know it was an accident.

knows.fact: Toby knows the name of every plant in the greenhouse.
Mr. Thorne grows a giant pumpkin called Goliath next door.

appearance: Toby is a boy with neat short hair.
He wears a club hoodie with a big front pocket.

mia.name: Mia
mia.personality: Bubbly, chatty and quick to giggle, but she goes quiet when she is embarrassed. Loyal to her friends; she sticks up for Toby.

demeanor.guarded: Friendly but a bit nervous. She worries she will be blamed because she watered Bertha last.

knows.fact: Mia and Toby are the gardening club's two pupils.

appearance: Mia is a girl with curly hair in a bouncy ponytail.
She wears the club's leaf-pattern wellies.

dobbs.name: Mr. Dobbs
dobbs.personality: Calm, slow-talking and kind, with a dry sense of humour. He likes everything tidy and written down.

demeanor.open: Friendly and helpful. He offers a cup of tea and answers plainly.

knows.fact: Mr. Dobbs is the school caretaker.
A fox keeps knocking over Mr. Dobbs's bins.

appearance: Mr. Dobbs is an old man in brown overalls.

thorne.name: Mr. Thorne
thorne.personality: Gruff, proud and easily offended, but not cruel. Under the grumbling he is a fair-minded gardener.

demeanor.guarded: Prickly and defensive. He has heard he is being blamed and is cross about it.
demeanor.shaken: Red-eared and huffy, but no longer shouting.
demeanor.cleared: Sheepish. Still gruff, but he wants the children's pumpkin done right by.

knows.fact: Mr. Thorne grows a giant pumpkin called Goliath.
Mr. Thorne has won many blue prize ribbons for his vegetables.

appearance: Mr. Thorne is a big man with a bushy grey beard.

clue_key_in_water_butt.fact: A key with a green tag reading GREENHOUSE lies at the bottom of the murky water butt by the door. It is the missing greenhouse key.

clue_ladder_tape.fact: A tall ladder leans on Mr. Thorne's side of the fence, right opposite the greenhouse. A tape measure dangles from its top rung.

hale_found_locked.fact: Ms. Hale says she unlocked the greenhouse door at half past seven. It was still locked, and Bertha was smashed inside.

hale_toby_fine.fact: Ms. Hale says Toby took losing his watering shifts well enough. He loves Bertha, and he would never hurt her.
hale_toby_fine.why: She is fond of Toby and feels guilty for being tough on him.

react_hale_gloves.fact: Ms. Hale twists the gardening gloves in her apron pocket, sighs, and says she won't have Toby made into a villain.

clue_hale_toby_upset.fact: Ms. Hale says she took Toby off the last watering shifts after he forgot to lock up on Monday, and told him no going in without a grown-up. Toby shouted, 'She's MY pumpkin!'

line.text: They promise to be fair to Toby, say something kind about him, or suggest it was an accident.

toby_alibi.fact: Toby says he was at home all Friday evening, finishing his thousand-piece jigsaw. He went to bed at nine.
toby_alibi.why: He is scared of getting into trouble.

react_toby_sweeping.fact: Toby's cheeks go pink and he sweeps the same patch of floor over and over.

react_toby_trainers.fact: Toby is wearing trainers on a muddy garden morning, while Mia wears her leaf-pattern club wellies. He tucks his feet out of sight.

toby_blames_thorne.fact: Toby says it was Mr. Thorne, who must have climbed over the fence and smashed the window to get in.
toby_blames_thorne.why: A burglar keeps eyes off him.

clue_toby_thorne_ladder.fact: Toby says that on Thursday Mr. Thorne was up his ladder, staring at Bertha with a tape measure. Mr. Thorne said, 'Enjoy her while she lasts!'

toby_no_key.fact: Toby says he has not seen the greenhouse key since Wednesday.

react_toby_pocket.fact: Toby's hand pats his hoodie pocket, as if checking for something that is not there.

clue_toby_mia_splat.fact: Toby says Mia said she wished Bertha would just go splat, so that she could get back to her dance practice.

toby_drops_burglar.fact: Toby admits that then nobody climbed in, and says maybe it was a fox.

toby_blames_mia.fact: Toby says Mia has leaf wellies too, and she had the last shifts, so it could just as well have been her.
toby_blames_mia.why: The evidence points at the club, and there are only two of them.

toby_not_mia.fact: Toby admits that then it was not Mia.

toby_confession.fact: Toby says he took the greenhouse key on Wednesday. He only went in to give Bertha extra water. He tripped on the hose, and the old bench fell on her. He broke the window so it would look like a burglar.

mia_alibi.fact: Mia says she watered Bertha at five with Mr. Dobbs's spare key, locked up and gave the key back. Then she helped her mum at the fair's cake tent from six till ten.

react_mia_pen.fact: When Mia talks about her watering shifts, she goes pink and clicks her sparkly purple pen on and off.

clue_mia_thorne_barbecue.fact: Mia says Mr. Thorne was at the growers' barbecue, right by her cake tent, all evening. At nine o'clock he bought carrot cake from her.

mia_admits_splat.fact: Mia admits she did say she wished Bertha would go splat, because she was fed up missing dance practice. She says she would never, ever hurt Bertha.

dobbs_rounds.fact: Mr. Dobbs says that on his eight o'clock rounds he shone his torch into the greenhouse. Bertha was whole, and the door was locked.

react_dobbs_slippers.fact: Mr. Dobbs rubs the back of his neck, glances at the garden window, and says he should have gone out last night, slippers or no slippers.

clue_dobbs_crash_time.fact: Mr. Dobbs says that at about ten to nine last night he heard a big thud from the garden, then smashing glass. He thought it was the fox at his bins again.

thorne_alibi.fact: Mr. Thorne says he was at the fair all evening with Goliath, at the growers' barbecue from seven till eleven.

clue_thorne_mia_cake.fact: Mr. Thorne says that at nine o'clock he bought carrot cake from young Mia at the fair's cake tent, across town. She was serving there from six till ten.

thorne_never_set_foot.fact: Mr. Thorne says he has never set foot in the school garden.
thorne_never_set_foot.why: He is embarrassed to have spied on a children's pumpkin.

react_thorne_boot.fact: Mr. Thorne's ears turn red and he scuffs one huge boot on the grass.

clue_thorne_measured.fact: Mr. Thorne admits he climbed over on Friday at four to measure Bertha through the window, and that the boot prints are his. He says Bertha was perfectly whole.

thorne_ladder_thursday.fact: Mr. Thorne says he measured Bertha from his ladder on Thursday, and that 'Enjoy her while she lasts' meant his Goliath would beat her at the weigh-in.

nobody_broke_in.text: Nobody broke in through the window. Whoever did it came through the locked door with a key.

thorne_cleared.text: Mr. Thorne is cleared: he was across town at the time of the crash.

prints_explained.text: The boot prints and ladder come from Mr. Thorne's measuring, not a break-in.

mia_cleared.text: Mia is cleared: she was serving cake across town at ten to nine.

rota_explained.text: The purple ink was Ms. Hale's doing. Mia never schemed for the shifts.

culprit_toby.text: Toby smashed Bertha by accident and faked the break-in.

motive.text: Bertha was Toby's pumpkin, and he was told to stay away from her.

how.text: The rotten bench collapsed onto Bertha. It was an accident.
